input.question: Why do we forget our dreams after waking up?
input.ground_truth: They aren't important to you. If you write them down or even mentally reevaluate them before you get out of bed or reorient yourself, you'll retain them better, but on a base level your brain prioritizes remembering real sense-data and clearing out or ignoring your "imagination."

Question: Why do we forget our dreams after waking up?

response.prediction: When we sleep, our brain creates fun stories called dreams. It's like playing with your toys. When you wake up, your brain switches to focusing on the real world, just like putting toys away to do something else. That's why we forget our dreams quickly, but sometimes a favorite part stays in our memory, like a favorite toy.

I remember when I was a kid, I thought of the brain as a big storage place. Maybe I can compare forgetting dreams to something they do every day, like playing with toys and then putting them away.

So, when we sleep, our brain is like a busy place where lots of things happen, including making up stories called dreams. When we wake up, the brain starts focusing on the real world again. It's like when you finish playing with your toys and put them away to do something else. The toys are still there, but you're not playing with them anymore.

In the case of dreams, the brain is so focused on the real world that it doesn't keep the dream stories active. That's why we forget them quickly. But sometimes, if we're really interested or if the dream was very strong, we might remember a little bit of it, just like how you might remember a favorite toy even after putting it away.

I should make sure the explanation is short and uses simple words. Maybe use an analogy they can relate to, like putting toys away or moving on to a new activity. That way, they can visualize why the brain stops holding onto the dream once they're awake.
